title: Scalar balancing respects ordinary etale open base change
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings. All schemes and morphisms below are arbitrary [def-pc-scheme]. Write $D_R(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $u_R^*$ for exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Use the canonical K-flat scalar/pullback isomorphism $\lambda_u:u_B^*Q_T\cong Q_Wu_A^*$ for $u:W\to T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], use exact extension by zero $j_{!,R}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $\beta_j:Q_Tj_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}Q_U$ be the balancing isomorphism of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Normalize its inverse by the open adjunction: $\beta_{j,M}^{-1}$ has transpose $\lambda_{j,j_{!,A}M}^{-1}\circ Q_U(\eta_{j,A,M})$, where $\eta_{j,A}$ is the unit [def-pur-open-coefficient-normalizations, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be arbitrary and put $U'=T'\times_TU$, with projections $h:U'\to U$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $R=A,B$, let $e_R:g_R^*j_{!,R}\cong j'_{!,R}h_R^*$ be the canonical degreewise open base-change isomorphism, whose inverse is the open adjunct of $h_R^*\eta_{j,R}$ after the square pullback identification [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]. Then, for every $M\in D_A(U)$,
$$j'_{!,B}(\lambda_{h,M})\circ e_{B,Q_UM}\circ g_B^*(\beta_{j,M})=\beta_{j',h_A^*M}\circ Q_{T'}(e_{A,M})\circ\lambda_{g,j_{!,A}M}.$$
Both maps go from $g_B^*Q_Tj_{!,A}M$ to $j'_{!,B}Q_{U'}h_A^*M$. The equation holds naturally on the entire derived category, with no boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 03S6, label lemma-shriek-base-change in etale-cohomology.tex; coefficient compatibility of its specified open-unit transpose

proof.text:
Write $L_R=j_{!,R}$, $J_R=j_R^*$, $L'_R=j'_{!,R}$, $J'_R=j_R'^*$, $G_R=g_R^*$ and $H_R=h_R^*$. Put $Q=Q_T$, $Q'=Q_{T'}$, $S=Q_U$, $S'=Q_{U'}$, $i=\beta_j^{-1}$, $i'=\beta_{j'}^{-1}$ and $d_R=e_R^{-1}$. Let $c_R:H_RJ_R\xrightarrow{\sim}J'_RG_R$ be the canonical square comparison. More explicitly, if $a_{v,u}:(vu)_R^*\cong u_R^*v_R^*$, then $c_R=a_{g,j'}a_{j,h}^{-1}$, using $jh=gj'$. The open tensor lemma supplies the adjunctions on the whole derived categories and the balancing isomorphisms. The prescribed transpose normalizations give
$$J_B(i_M)\eta_{B,SM}=\lambda_{j,L_AM}^{-1}S(\eta_{A,M}),\qquad
J'_B(i'_V)\eta'_{B,S'V}=\lambda_{j',L'_AV}^{-1}S'(\eta'_{A,V}),$$
$$J'_R(d_{R,M})\eta'_{R,H_RM}=c_{R,L_RM}H_R(\eta_{R,M}).$$
Here $V\in D_A(U')$, and juxtaposition composes right to left. The last identity is precisely the unit formula for the inverse base-change mate; its degreewise version descends with the normalized exact open adjunction. These identities specify the actual maps, without claiming that pullback alone detects equality.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change; explicit coefficient/unit calculation for the specified inverse open mate, written by N7.

proof.text:
Apply scalar/pullback composition coherence to $(j,h)$ and to $(g,j')$, for an arbitrary $N\in D_A(T)$. Both composite scheme maps equal $k=jh=gj'$. For either pair $(v,u)$, that coherence says
$$\lambda_{u,v_A^*N}\,u_B^*(\lambda_{v,N})\,a_{v,u,B,QN}=Q_{\mathrm{source}(u)}(a_{v,u,A,N})\lambda_{k,N}.$$
Substitute the two pairs and eliminate the common $\lambda_{k,N}$. With $c_R=a_{g,j'}a_{j,h}^{-1}$, this gives
$$\lambda_{j',G_AN}J'_B(\lambda_{g,N})c_{B,QN}=S'(c_{A,N})\lambda_{h,J_AN}H_B(\lambda_{j,N}).$$
Multiply by the inverse scalar comparisons, to obtain the form needed below:
$$J'_B(\lambda_{g,N}^{-1})\lambda_{j',G_AN}^{-1}S'(c_{A,N})=c_{B,QN}H_B(\lambda_{j,N}^{-1})\lambda_{h,J_AN}^{-1}.\tag{*}$$
All the cited comparisons are the canonical exact-pullback transports of the K-flat comparisons used in the statement. The composition theorem explicitly allows arbitrary unbounded objects and arbitrary coefficient ring maps.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change; explicit coefficient/unit calculation for the specified inverse open mate, written by N7.

proof.text:
Fix $M\in D_A(U)$. The inverses of the two isomorphisms in the asserted equation are the following maps from $L'_BS'H_AM$ to $G_BQL_AM$:
$$x=G_B(i_M)d_{B,SM}L'_B(\lambda_{h,M}^{-1}),\qquad
y=\lambda_{g,L_AM}^{-1}Q'(d_{A,M})i'_{H_AM}.$$
These formulas follow just by reversing the order of each composite and replacing its factors by their inverses. Under $L'_B\dashv J'_B$, the transpose of a map $z:L'_BS'H_AM\to G_BQL_AM$ is $z^\flat=J'_B(z)\eta'_{B,S'H_AM}$. It therefore suffices to show $x^\flat=y^\flat$.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change; explicit coefficient/unit calculation for the specified inverse open mate, written by N7.

proof.text:
Compute $x^\flat$. Naturality of $\eta'_B$ moves $L'_B(\lambda_h^{-1})$ across the unit, and the unit formula for $d_B$ from step 1 then gives
$$x^\flat=J'_BG_B(i_M)c_{B,L_BSM}H_B(\eta_{B,SM})\lambda_{h,M}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $c_B$ at $i_M$ and then the first identity of step 1 give
$$x^\flat=c_{B,QL_AM}H_B(\lambda_{j,L_AM}^{-1})H_BS(\eta_{A,M})\lambda_{h,M}^{-1}.$$
Finally, naturality of $\lambda_h^{-1}:S'H_A\to H_BS$ at $\eta_{A,M}:M\to J_AL_AM$ yields
$$x^\flat=c_{B,QL_AM}H_B(\lambda_{j,L_AM}^{-1})\lambda_{h,J_AL_AM}^{-1}S'H_A(\eta_{A,M}).\tag{1}$$
Each equality is substitution of a specified transpose formula or naturality of a specified natural transformation.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change; explicit coefficient/unit calculation for the specified inverse open mate, written by N7.

proof.text:
For $y$, insert the transpose formula for $i'$:
$$y^\flat=J'_B(\lambda_{g,L_AM}^{-1})J'_BQ'(d_{A,M})\lambda_{j',L'_AH_AM}^{-1}S'(\eta'_{A,H_AM}).$$
Naturality of $\lambda_{j'}^{-1}:S'J'_A\to J'_BQ'$ at $d_{A,M}:L'_AH_AM\to G_AL_AM$ rewrites the last three factors as $\lambda_{j',G_AL_AM}^{-1}S'(J'_A(d_{A,M})\eta'_{A,H_AM})$. The unit formula for $d_A$ from step 1 thus gives
$$y^\flat=J'_B(\lambda_{g,L_AM}^{-1})\lambda_{j',G_AL_AM}^{-1}S'(c_{A,L_AM})S'H_A(\eta_{A,M}).\tag{2}$$
This uses only the two unit normalizations and naturality, and never assumes that $Q'$ is exact on sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change; explicit coefficient/unit calculation for the specified inverse open mate, written by N7.

proof.text: Use $(*)$ at $N=L_AM$ and precompose it with $S'H_A(\eta_{A,M})$. Equations (1) and (2) are then identical, so $x^\flat=y^\flat$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives $x=y$; taking inverses proves the required equation. Every factor and every equality used is natural in $M$, hence the equality is one of natural transformations. The calculation takes place entirely in the ordinary unbounded derived categories furnished by the cited open tensor lemma and scalar-composition theorem. Thus no restriction on cohomological degrees, no flatness of $B$ over $A$, and no quasi-compactness of $j$ or $g$ is introduced.
